title: Production of Bacterial Cellulose by Gluconacetobacter hansenii Using Corn Steep Liquor As Nutrient Sources
access: open (Frontiers PDF read; the PMC page blocks automated fetch)
licence_stated: CC BY (read from the paper; verify)
extraction_status: full (Tables 1-4; no figure-only data needed for yields)
vegan_study_note: HS control and Media 1, 2, 5, 6, 9 carry peptone (origin unspecified; Merck): flagged. Medium 3 and Alt. media 10-18 use corn steep liquor and no peptone or yeast extract: clear. Effluent media flagged for unitemised composition
wa_study_note: glucose and molasses: yes; corn steep liquor: unknown (regional supply not checked); jeans laundry effluent tested and gave no BC
notes: Nine screening media (Tables 1 and 3), then a nine-run glucose x CSL grid (Tables 2 and 4); the layout resembles a central composite design with one centre point, but the paper does not name it (inference). Best: 15 g/L glucose + 25 g/L CSL at 9.63 g/L dry versus 8.00 for HS; the paper's 73% claim is on hydrated mass. Wet:dry ratio varies 25-118 across media, so hydrated mass is not a proxy. Thickness statements conflict (0.62 mm; 0.2-0.5 mm; 8.7 mm hydrated; 0.48 mm dried). Properties (crystallinity, TGA, tensile) are in the text but parked to pass 2.
